docs.title: A guide to sources, with evidence attached
docs.text:
Every card links to the original publisher and records what was checked. Free access does not necessarily permit redistribution. Registration and research approval are separate from technical formats such as CSV, Stata or an API.

This is a manually curated starting point, not a complete inventory of UN statistics or survey variables. No statistical observations or respondent files are stored here. Read the coverage notes, access guide and research guides before comparing sources.

The header search searches the full documentation. The finder above combines metadata search with filters. You can share a filtered search by copying its URL.

docs.title: Access guide
docs.text:
Access describes the route to data, not the file format or reuse license.

Code Meaning In available free data? OPEN No-fee data without an account; terms may still apply Yes REGISTER Free registration or user form; no substantive research review Yes APPLY No-fee research application or authorization; approval not guaranteed Yes, conditionally REQUEST Individually supplied data with a confirmed no-fee policy Yes, conditionally METADATA_ONLY Only discovery/documentation is established by this card No; reference directory only PAID Purchase, subscription or paid license required No

The initial records do not need to contain an example of every code. In particular, we do not invent a REQUEST or PAID example to fill a category. PAID remains in the schema so future reviews can explicitly reject or track out-of-scope leads without exposing them as available free data.

Methods (api, bulk_download, web_download, web_interface, research_application, email_request) and formats (CSV, JSON, SDMX, Stata, SPSS, etc.) are separate. An API can require registration. A catalogue may expose DDI metadata while withholding the respondent file.

Read the scope of the access claim. Afrobarometer public survey files are distinct from any special geocoded products. Global Findex public records do not provide the full Gallup World Poll. UNHCR aggregate statistics do not establish access to its microdata library. National restricted MTUS files may have additional conditions.

license_url points to the provider's documented access/terms evidence. Where a uniform license was not established, license_name says so instead of inventing an open license. Cite the selected release and follow its attribution, research-only and non-redistribution conditions. The repository license covers only our original code and metadata prose.

docs.text:
Discovery portals can include restricted or unavailable studies. A METADATA_ONLY entry is never a confirmed free dataset.

  • FAOSTAT — Catalog; OPEN. Food, agriculture, land, inputs and agrifood emissions data.
  • IHSN Survey Catalog — Catalog; METADATA_ONLY. Meta-catalog of household surveys and censuses, directing users to study documentation and custodians.
  • UN System Data Commons — Catalog; METADATA_ONLY. Cross-agency discovery portal for UN-system statistics. Start here to locate sources, then check the original publisher.
  • United Nations Treaty Collection — Catalog; OPEN. Treaty texts and depositary information on international commitments. Useful for affiliation research, but not a ready-made alliance panel.
  • UNdata statistical databases — Catalog; OPEN. UN data retrieval portal with statistical datamarts and downloadable tables. Republishes statistics from multiple producers.
  • UNODC Data Portal — Catalog; OPEN. Crime, drugs, violence, justice and related SDG statistics.
  • World Bank Data Catalog — Catalog; METADATA_ONLY. Discovery across development datasets and contributing catalogs.
  • World Bank Microdata Library — Catalog; METADATA_ONLY. Study-level survey documentation and access routes, including LSMS and Global Findex.

docs.title: Coverage and limitations
docs.text:
The seed was reviewed on 7 November 2026. It demonstrates the architecture and all fourteen topic groups; it is not a full census of organizations, datasets, countries or questions.

Included examples cover UNdata, UN System Data Commons, the SDG database, World Bank catalogs and indicators, ILOSTAT, WHO GHO, FAOSTAT, UNODC, UNHCR, MICS, IPUMS MICS, LSMS, Global Findex, WVS, ESS, ISSP, Afrobarometer and MTUS. Not every represented organization is a UN agency: source cards explain the relationship.

Current limits:

  • Broad statistical databases coexist with specific survey releases, and are explicitly labeled. Search counts are metadata records, never counts of independent underlying studies.
  • Country tags cover only checked examples. Most portals' country inventories have not been enumerated. Filter results should not be interpreted as exhaustive availability.
  • Defense, alliance membership, diplomatic relations, noise pollution, light pollution and several other subtopics remain thin or absent. The treaty collection is useful primary material for A5, not a harmonized alliance panel.
  • No full indicator/question dictionary, cross-country comparability scoring, complete wave inventory, or download authentication test has been performed.
  • Some landing pages require JavaScript or use dynamic links. Cards favor stable official landing/documentation URLs; APIs are labeled documentation or examples, not promises of tested uptime.
  • The site performs local metadata search. It does not query provider APIs in the background, update itself, collect analytics or send search terms to a data provider.
  • A successful static build and functional checks do not replace a full browser and screen-reader accessibility audit. Visual browser QA was unavailable during the initial build.

The initial implementation has no workflows, schedules, crawlers, imports or background synchronization. Local rendering commands are run manually, only against the already-authored YAML.

docs.title: Scope and unit of cataloging
docs.text:
The atlas covers freely accessible UN-system data, documented collaborations and independent international survey datasets. It is a metadata directory; it does not host statistical observations or respondent data. “Open” in the project title includes documented no-fee registration and application routes; it does not mean every source has an open license.

Four record kinds form a graph:

  1. Organization / source: institutional identity and relationship to the UN.
  2. Catalog: portal or meta-catalog indexing resources. Some also distribute data.
  3. Programme: recurring survey or harmonization programme.
  4. Dataset: a statistical database family or a specific survey release. The title and release field say which.

A parent relationship expresses the main catalog/programme context. catalog_ids expresses additional discovery locations. The same study is not duplicated just because it appears in IHSN and the World Bank. A harmonized derivative such as IPUMS MICS gets its own record linked to the original programme; it is not a new independent survey. A variable/indicator entity is intentionally deferred.

docs.title: Institutions and provenance
docs.text:
organization_id links to the responsible source card. original_producer, collector and publisher describe distinct roles. National statistical agencies frequently produce data that international organizations harmonize and publish. Broad database cards name the producer class; precise producer identifiers belong in future series-level records.

UN_SYSTEM includes UN entities and autonomous specialized institutions. UN_RELATED is reserved for documented formal related-organization status. UN_PARTNER requires evidence of a particular collaboration and does not imply UN ownership. INDEPENDENT prevents research networks from being mislabeled as UN bodies merely because UN publications use their data. Membership context comes from the CEB; individual partner claims have card-specific evidence.

docs.title: Two dimensions, not two competing copies
docs.text:
The source directory and the topic directory are rendered from the same curated YAML records. Topics can overlap. Country and microdata topics are discovery routes; they are not a claim that every linked item has the same unit of observation. For example, a treaty has a treaty/event unit, and Findex has separate individual and aggregate products.

data_levels describes publication form. observation_units describes what one observation refers to. A household sampling frame does not automatically make the public file household-level. MTUS diary-day records require additional care. Neither topic nor programme membership substitutes for these fields.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Each card records a check date, evidence URLs, supported claims and verification scope. verified in this seed means official public documentation was reviewed; it does not mean we created an account, received research approval, downloaded every data file or audited every variable. discovered is for unverified leads; indexed is reserved for deeper release/series indexing. Neither status guarantees freshness.

Provider documentation can conflict or lag an interface. The WVS access note explains a discrepancy between older no-registration publicity and current registration documentation. The Ethiopia LSMS seed is marked reference-only because its current public access page did not establish data availability. Failures to fetch JavaScript pages are not interpreted as proof that data are unavailable.

docs.title: Geography and time
docs.text:
Country tags are confirmed examples, not the full coverage. Their completeness is explicit. No country match is inferred from a worldwide programme label. This conservative filter has false negatives until the inventory expands. A record can be globally scoped yet contain no country codes in this release.

Time coverage is descriptive at this stage. A programme's starting date must not be mistaken for a balanced panel. Dataset release, fieldwork year and publication date are different. Geography, variable availability, sampling and weights should be verified at the original source before analysis.

docs.text:

docs.title: Manual editing and publishing
docs.text: There are no GitHub Actions workflows, imports, scheduled checks or deploy bots in this repository. The rendered HTML is committed in docs/, so GitHub Pages can serve it without installing Python or MkDocs.

docs.title: Enable GitHub Pages
docs.text:
Open repository Settings → Pages → Build and deployment. Choose Deploy from a branch, then main and /docs, and save. GitHub's built-in Pages publication service may show a deployment run; that is the hosting mechanism, not a repository-defined data pipeline. The .nojekyll file preserves MkDocs output.

Expected address: Open Global Data Atlas. The root README and source Markdown remain usable if Pages is not enabled.

Reference: GitHub publishing-source documentation.

docs.title: Edit locally
docs.text:
Use Python 3.10 or later. Install the pinned build dependencies in an isolated environment:

python -m venv .venv
# Activate .venv for your operating system.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

Edit catalog/, taxonomy/, crosswalks/ or the editorial pages under wiki/. Then explicitly run:

python scripts/validate.py
python scripts/render_catalog.py
python -m mkdocs build --strict
python scripts/check_site.py
node scripts/test_search.cjs

Review the changed metadata, generated pages, exports and compiled docs/, then commit and push them together. Site rebuilding is manual. These local helpers do not access the network or harvest data. If deleting a record, also remove its old generated page from wiki/records/ before building; validation checks for stale pages at the site-check stage.

For an optional local preview, run python -m mkdocs serve. Plainly opening HTML using file:// can prevent the browser from loading the local JSON search index; use HTTP or GitHub Pages.

Public URLs in mkdocs.yml need adjustment if the repository is forked to another owner. Authored content is English. Prefer stable official links, preserve IDs, explain access discrepancies and attach evidence before calling an entry verified.

docs.title: Compare social trust
docs.text: Start with WVS, ESS, ISSP or Afrobarometer. Locate the precise question and response scale. Interpersonal trust, trust in government and confidence in a particular institution are distinct constructs. Check country participation, translation, response options and fieldwork year before pooling. Use the design and population weights appropriate to the estimand. A survey average is not automatically an official country indicator.

docs.title: Find financial behaviour or household budgets
docs.text: Global Findex measures adults' financial inclusion and reported use of services. It is not a household expenditure diary. Explore LSMS and the IHSN catalog for household consumption studies, then confirm that the specific study has an accessible release. Keep person, household and household-member files distinct. Compare recall periods, price adjustments, household definitions and survey weights.

docs.title: Compare time use and unpaid care
docs.text: Start with MTUS and its user guide. Identify the diary unit, age universe, day-of-week coverage and handling of simultaneous activities. National diary instruments and activity groupings differ. A harmonized category does not remove all design differences. Mapping unpaid-care diaries to SDG 5.4.1 requires a compatible numerator, denominator and population; the crosswalk deliberately marks this as a potential input.

docs.title: Connect household survey files
docs.text: MICS may publish household, member, women and child files under one survey. Use the documented keys and file-specific weights. Verify universes before joining: a household characteristic is not an additional independent individual response. IPUMS MICS can simplify harmonization, but sample differences still matter.

docs.title: Follow international commitments
docs.text: Use the UN Treaty Collection for treaty texts, depositary notices and status evidence. A signature, ratification and entry into force are different events. Treaty participation does not imply an alliance, and current status does not by itself reconstruct a historical panel. Record the event definition and effective date before turning documents into country-level variables.

docs.title: Staged next steps
docs.text:
Nothing on this page is enabled or scheduled.

Before adding long-lived build automation, review the theme lifecycle. The requested Material for MkDocs implementation is pinned and working, but its maintainers announce end of life on May 5, 2027. Evaluate a supported migration while retaining the portable YAML/Markdown catalog; no framework migration is included in this release.

  1. Expand and review the registry manually. Fill source gaps, add complete country/wave coverage, verify download routes and nominate maintainers. Prioritize diplomacy/defense, time use, household budgets, environmental exposures and missing UN agencies. Add reproducible issue templates for access corrections.
  2. Add validation on proposed changes, if approved. Run schema, relationship, export consistency and internal-link checks on pull requests. Keep external link checks rate-limited and distinguish temporary blocking from dead resources. This stage does not import data.
  3. Pilot one metadata-only importer. Start with a well-documented catalog such as the World Bank Indicators API or ILOSTAT table of contents. Cache metadata, retain provenance and revisions, use stable IDs, and submit changes for human review. Do not download respondent files or bypass registration. Review each provider's automation terms first; UNHCR's current API guidance specifically limits continuous/high-volume extraction and production backend use.
  4. Index studies, indicators and questions. Model release-specific countries, years, units, question wording, response scales and file relationships. Build conservative duplicate links and distinguish harmonized derivatives. Extend the schema before ingesting variable-level metadata.
  5. Introduce opt-in scheduled refreshes only after pilots work. Set a modest cadence, failure budget, rate limits, change summaries and human approval thresholds. Preserve historic metadata snapshots and an audit trail. Schedule publishing separately from metadata discovery, and keep licensing changes visible.

Provider APIs and catalogs have different terms and structures; a universal crawler is not the recommended first step. Success should be measured by accurate access routes and useful study discovery before expanding record counts.

docs.title: Schema reference · version 1.0
docs.text: The canonical records are UTF-8 YAML files under catalog/{organizations,catalogs,programs,datasets}/. The JSON Schema uses Draft 2020-12, rejects unknown fields and is enforced by the manually run validator. IDs are globally unique lowercase kebab-case strings. Relationships use IDs, not names.

docs.title: Shared fields
docs.text: Field Type Contract schema_version string Exactly 1.0 id string Stable globally unique ID; filename matches kind enum organization, catalog, program, dataset name, description string English human-readable label and summary topics string array Zero or more of A1–A6 and B1–B8; organizations may have an empty list keywords string array English discovery terms and common aliases verification object Status, date, method, scope, nonempty evidence list

docs.text:
Field Type Contract website URL Official home or programme-specific organization page un_relation enum UN_SYSTEM, UN_RELATED, UN_PARTNER, INDEPENDENT relation_note string Explain legal independence or the particular collaboration; evidence required

Organizations have no implicit dataset access status. Source cards list their linked resources.

docs.text: Field Type Contract organization_id ID Must resolve to an organization parent_id ID or null Primary parent catalog or programme; no cycles catalog_ids ID array Additional indexing catalogs; no duplicate dataset records original_producer string Who creates or harmonizes data; national agencies may differ by series collector string Who collected responses or administrative records publisher string Who distributes this representation; may differ from the responsible organization data_levels enum array aggregate, microdata, geospatial, text_event observation_units enum array country, region, person, household, diary_day, treaty, event, organization, firm, grid_cell geography object Scope, regions, country codes, completeness and explanatory notes time_coverage string Descriptive fieldwork/series coverage, without implying a balanced panel release string or null Exact release identifier where verified; null if not pinned access object Data access status, fee availability flag, methods, formats, notes and terms reference links object array Each has rel and exact url; first is the original landing URL survey object or null Method, weights, representativeness, comparability; required non-null for survey programme/dataset microdata

docs.title: Geography
docs.text: scope is single_country, multi_country or global. regions uses the discovery regions in taxonomy/geography.yml, not a claimed official UN M49 hierarchy. country_codes uses the curated ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 examples in that file. Territories and non-ISO provider geographies require an explicit future schema extension; never silently rewrite a provider code as ISO. coverage_completeness is complete, partial or not_enumerated. notes explains what was checked. Empty codes mean unknown/not enumerated, never “no coverage.”

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
status is OPEN, REGISTER, APPLY, REQUEST, METADATA_ONLY or PAID. free_data_available must be true for the first four and false for the last two. For APPLY/REQUEST, true describes a documented no-fee route, not approval for a particular user. The UI starts with available free routes only.

methods and formats use taxonomy/methods.yml. notes limits the claim to the actual product. license_name is a provider license name when established, otherwise an explicit provider-specific/unknown statement. license_url links to the provider terms or access documentation; it is not a blanket relicensing claim.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: status: discovered, verified, indexed. checked_on: ISO date. method: public_documentation or download_test. scope: what was and was not checked. evidence: nonempty array of {url, claim} objects. Official provider documentation supports access claims, but public-documentation verification does not imply successful authenticated download.

docs.title: SDG crosswalk
docs.text: crosswalks/sdg-indicators.csv has record_id, topic_id, goal, target, indicator, mapping_type, note, evidence_url. Goal/target/indicator identifiers are strings. mapping_type is official_series, related_measure or potential_input. Relationships are many-to-many. SDG codes are not valid topic IDs. Crosswalk edits require checking the current official metadata, because indicator frameworks are revised.

docs.title: Export and search contract
docs.text:
JSONL exports complete canonical records, one JSON object per line. CSV uses the union of top-level fields as columns; nested arrays/objects are compact JSON strings in properly quoted CSV cells. Blank means the field is absent for that entity kind; literal null means an explicitly null canonical value. For lossless processing prefer JSONL.

The browser index adds organization_name, un_relation, topic_labels, country_labels and card_url as derived display fields. These do not belong in canonical YAML. It excludes organization rows because they have a separate source directory. The search count is a count of heterogeneous metadata records.

Validation checks structural types, known topics/countries, foreign keys, parent cycles, free-data rules and SDG references. Site checks also verify export equivalence, generated record consistency and local links. These are manually invoked checks, not scheduled automation.

docs.title: SDG crosswalk
docs.text:
SDGs are a policy framework, separate from the 14 discovery topics. The framework is not a mutually exclusive or exhaustive taxonomy of all UN data: goals overlap, indicators may repeat across targets, and many statistical series lie outside the framework. Do not sum unlike indicators into a single score.

The mappings below are curated examples. Official series, related measure and potential input mean different things. Potential inputs require a compatible population, definition, denominator and calculation. No mapping alone establishes statistical equivalence or custodianship.
